name: Henry of Bolingbroke
description: The fourteen-year-old son of John of Gaunt, present in the Tower of London when rebels overran it on 14 June 1381. Chronicle tradition holds that he was discovered and about to be killed -- as Gaunt's son -- when a royal guard, John Ferrour, successfully intervened on his behalf. He would depose Richard II eighteen years later and reign as Henry IV; that later history is outside this book's scope, but the near-miss at the Tower is one of the revolt's sharper ironies given what both boys in this book -- Richard and Henry -- would become to each other.
narrative_function: A near-casualty at the Tower whose survival has outsized long-run consequences well beyond 1381.
